focus: Qwen Code: hooks, tool names, install/update/rollback, compaction path, deny/rewrite/replace, subagent handling, project source, skills, v1 footprint

findings.title: Qwen Code DOES have a PreCompact hook, contradicting ADR-0009's compaction delivery table
findings.claim: ADR-0009-compaction-and-memory.md:95 states: 'Claude Code, Codex, Qwen, ZCode | computed inside SessionStart(compact). No PreCompact hook, no precomputing'. For Qwen Code this is false.
findings.evidence: qwen-code source (pinned 18f80f5, per TECH-SPEC.md:18) has a real, wired PreCompact hook: packages/core/src/hooks/hookEventHandler.ts:615-631 defines firePreCompactEvent(trigger, instructions) which builds a PreCompactInput and fires HookEventName.PreCompact. It is called from packages/core/src/services/chatCompressionService.ts:603 and packages/core/src/config/config.ts:4418, i.e. before compaction runs, not dead code. hookPlanner.ts:62 and hook-event-display.ts:67 also carry a PreCompact case for Qwen's hook pipeline.
findings.regression_risk: If v2's compaction-memory design assumes Qwen has no PreCompact hook and relies solely on SessionStart(compact) to inject state, it will miss the PreCompact moment Qwen actually exposes, or double-fire logic if a future contributor adds a PreCompact handler assuming none exists. The ADR's own 'no precomputing' claim for Qwen is also at risk: a real PreCompact hook means precomputing before compaction is possible for Qwen, same family as the Gemini/Copilot/VS Code row.
findings.fix: Correct ADR-0009's table: move Qwen out of the 'No PreCompact hook' row. Verify whether Qwen's PreCompact hook receives enough context to write state before compaction (same pattern as the Gemini/Copilot CLI/VS Code row: write `meta('pending_compact:'+sid)` and consume on next prompt), or document explicitly why SessionStart(compact) is still preferred over the available PreCompact hook for Qwen specifically.

findings.title: Qwen tool-name and extension-install claims in TECH-SPEC/README/ADR-0011 are correct and verified — no new finding, confirming prior review did not flag a real gap here
findings.claim: TECH-SPEC.md:191 'Qwen Code | mcp__context-mode__ctx_execute | packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts:1209,1241' and README.md:53 / ADR-0011:42 'Gemini, Qwen | extensions install <url> --ref release' (with --auto-update).
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts:1238-1239 names the tool via generateValidName(`mcp__${serverName}__${serverToolName}`), matching the doc's claimed shape. packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/install.ts:30-31,55,171-176,210-211 defines both --ref and --auto-update as real, wired CLI options; packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/uninstall.ts:45-47 confirms an uninstall path exists for the v1-entry-removal step ADR-0011:42 assumes.
findings.regression_risk: None — this is a confirmation, not a contradiction.
findings.fix: No doc change needed for this specific claim.

findings.title: No rollback command found in Qwen Code's extension system — ADR-0011's v1→v2 transition plan for Qwen has no verified rollback path
findings.claim: ADR-0011-release-and-v1-transition.md:42 describes the forward install path for Qwen ('remove the v1 MCP entry, then gemini/qwen extensions install ... --ref release --auto-update') but names no rollback command if the v2 extension install fails or a regression is found post-install.
findings.evidence: Searching packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/*.ts in the qwen-code source turned up install.ts, uninstall.ts, update.ts, list.ts — no rollback.ts, no --rollback flag, and no revert-to-previous-ref option in install.ts's option list (ref, auto-update only). A rollback today would mean uninstall + manual re-install of the old v1 MCP entry by hand, which ADR-0011 does not document as a step or a tested path.
findings.regression_risk: If a v2 release breaks Qwen users, the documented transition path has only a one-way install step; without a rollback command or documented manual steps, an owner-decided 'frequent releases, no signing' policy (per DECISIONS-r3) increases exposure, because every release is undoable only by hand for Qwen users.
findings.fix: Add an explicit rollback step for Qwen/Gemini in ADR-0011: either document the manual re-add of the v1 MCP entry (config path + exact JSON), or confirm there truly is no CLI-native rollback and call that out as a known limitation with a support runbook reference.

method: git-archaeology-not-applicable-shallow-clone: qwen-code scratchpad clone at 18f80f5 is a 1-commit shallow checkout (git log --oneline | wc -l == 1), so --follow/-S archaeology against qwen-code's own history was not possible; findings instead verified directly against the pinned source tree, matching TECH-SPEC.md:18's stated pin.
summary: 1 blocker (PreCompact hook mischaracterized for Qwen in ADR-0009), 1 major (no verified rollback path for Qwen in ADR-0011), 1 confirmation (tool-name/install-flag claims hold up).
